title: Iterate Wronskians over $\mathbb{R}^d$ as $N$-ary brackets on $\mathbb{R}[x^1,\ldots,x^d]$: the $N$-bonacci numbers bound the highest total degrees
summary: For the algebra $\mathbb{R}[x^1,\ldots,x^d]$ of polynomials in $d\geqslant 1$ variables, regard the complete generalised Wronskian $W_d^k$ of differential order $k\geqslant 1$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$ as the $N=\tbinom{d+k}{d}$-ary Lie bracket. Take an $N$-tuple of polynomials, calculate their Wronskian, and keep re-using the newly-created polynomials to produce more of them. The problem is: how fast do their maximal total degrees grow with the number $n$ of iterations of the bracket?
